title: Improving order history search using semantic search with Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: Amazon's Your Orders team added semantic search on top of keyword search so generic queries find related past purchases, with embeddings from a model hosted on SageMaker.
Uses exact k-NN scoped to one customer's orders plus hybrid ranking, backfills historical orders, and rolls out gradually.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon SageMaker
authors: Amazon — Shwetabh ., Ayush Kumar, Harshavardhan Miryala

title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless introduces collection groups to optimize cost for multi-tenant workloads
key_points: OpenSearch Serverless collection groups let collections with different KMS keys share compute, so per-tenant encryption no longer needs dedicated capacity per key.
Adds minimum capacity per group for steady performance and maximum capacity as a spending cap.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, AWS KMS
authors: Madhusudhan Narayana, Prashant Agrawal, Xian Huang

title: How Swiss Life Germany automated data governance and collaboration with Amazon SageMaker
key_points: Swiss Life Germany runs SageMaker Unified Studio as a federated platform: a management account with no data, and data and compute in each IT system's own accounts with DEV/TEST/PROD stages.
Where Terraform lacked SageMaker resources, the team wrapped API calls in Lambda functions invoked by Terraform with create/update/delete lifecycle, keeping everything in state.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Terraform, AWS Lambda
authors: Swiss Life Germany — Tim Kopacz, Benjamin Westphal, Lakshmi Nair

title: Implement a data mesh pattern in Amazon SageMaker Catalog without changing applications
key_points: Uses SageMaker Catalog's publish/subscribe across producer and consumer accounts while the existing S3 data, Glue catalog tables and a Lambda consumer stay as they are.

The producer brings its own Glue tables into a project via Lake Formation grants; after subscription, the consumer Lambda's IAM role is given the subscribed access instead of running inside a project.
Long three-account setup; useful as the pattern for retrofitting a data mesh onto existing workloads.
services: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS Lake Formation, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Lambda, Amazon S3
decision: Move producers and consumers into catalog projects vs keep existing apps and grant subscribed access to their own roles
authors: Paolo Romagnoli, Joel Farvault

title: How CyberArk uses Apache Iceberg and Amazon Bedrock to deliver up to 4x support productivity
key_points: CyberArk dropped a multi-step pipeline (parse on Fargate, convert to Parquet, wait for Glue crawlers) for one Fargate step that writes Iceberg tables directly with PyIceberg, so uploaded logs are queryable in Athena at once without Spark or crawlers.

For unseen log formats, Bedrock generates grok parsing patterns from samples; they are validated on more samples and stored in DynamoDB for reuse. Agents then investigate support cases over the tables.
AWS reports up to 95% shorter case resolution time and up to 4x support productivity; Glue automatic table optimisation handles compaction.
services: Apache Iceberg, PyIceberg, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Fargate, Amazon Athena, AWS Glue, Amazon DynamoDB
decision: Parquet + crawler pipeline vs writing Iceberg directly with PyIceberg (no Spark) for small, varied file ingestion
attaches_to: aws-bytes: File Layout Optimization (active); GenAI on data / lakehouse (later)
authors: CyberArk — Moshiko Ben Abu, Riki Nizri, Sofie Zilberman

title: Best practices for right-sizing Amazon OpenSearch Service domains
key_points: Uses CloudWatch metrics to tell an under-provisioned OpenSearch domain (CPU, JVM pressure, rejections) from an over-provisioned one, with fixes for each.
Recommends baselines, regular reviews, shard and storage tuning, and alarms for traffic spikes.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon CloudWatch
authors: Nikhil Agarwal, Arun Lakshmanan, Rick Balwani

title: Build a data pipeline from Google Search Console to Amazon Redshift using AWS Glue
key_points: Glue has a native Google Search Console connector: OAuth client in Google Cloud, secret in Secrets Manager, then a visual ETL job writes Sites, Sitemaps or Search Analytics data into Redshift tables.
Search Analytics accepts filter predicates (date range, device, country, grouping dimensions) pushed to the API.
Console-only walkthrough with no schema mapping or incremental loading.
services: AWS Glue, Amazon Redshift, AWS Secrets Manager, Google Search Console
decision: Native Glue SaaS connector vs custom API ingestion for marketing/SaaS data into Redshift
authors: Anirudh Chawla, Prabhu G, Shubham Purwar, Shaswat Mandhanya

title: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink application lifecycle management with Terraform
key_points: Manages a Managed Flink application with Terraform: create, code and config changes, scaling, runtime upgrades, and what happens when a change breaks state compatibility with system rollback on.
Lists operations Terraform cannot do, such as stopping/starting without a config change or restoring from an older snapshot.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, Terraform
authors: Felix John, Mazrim Mehrtens

title: Verisk cuts processing time and storage costs with Amazon Redshift and lakehouse
key_points: Verisk moved catastrophe-model analytics from on-premises databases to Redshift Serverless querying Parquet and Iceberg on S3, in three stages: pre-process in Redshift, model on AWS Batch, aggregate back in Redshift.
Iceberg is used only where it pays off: versioned datasets needing schema changes and point-in-time reconstruction for audit.
Multi-tenant isolation is a schema per client plus Redshift metadata security, with dedicated clusters only for the largest tenants; stored procedures standardise the aggregations.
services: Amazon Redshift Serverless, Apache Iceberg, Amazon S3, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Batch, Amazon Quick Sight, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse
decision: Schema-per-tenant with metadata security vs cluster-per-tenant for a multi-tenant warehouse; Parquet vs Iceberg per dataset
authors: Verisk — Karthick Shanmugam, Srinivasa Are, Duvan Segura-Camelo, Ashish Agrawal, Raks Khare

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service 101: T-shirt size your domain for e-commerce search
key_points: Sizes OpenSearch domains for read-heavy e-commerce product search in XS to XL bands based on catalog size and query concurrency.
Covers storage planning, shard strategy, scaling with replicas, load testing and monitoring.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon CloudWatch
authors: Abe Raghib, Aditya Challa, Harsh Bansal, Raaga N.G

title: Common streaming data enrichment patterns in Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
key_points: Six ways to enrich a stream with reference data in Managed Flink: load it all into task memory, load only each partition's share into keyed state, reload that state periodically, async lookup per record, async lookup through an external cache, or a Table API join.
Compares them on latency, throughput, freshness when reference data changes, memory use and complexity; the right one depends mostly on reference-data size and how often it changes.
Updated version of a 2024 post, with code on GitHub.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, Apache Flink
decision: Pre-load vs keyed-state pre-load vs async lookup (with or without cache) vs Table API join for stream enrichment
authors: Ali Alemi, Felix John, Sam Mokhtari, Subham Rakshit

title: Matching your Ingestion Strategy with your OpenSearch Query Patterns
key_points: Explains index analyzers and builds a custom edge n-gram analyzer so autocomplete becomes a cheap term match at query time instead of a wildcard query.
General point: decide the query patterns before designing the index.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service
authors: Rakan Kandah

title: Amazon Athena adds 1-minute reservations and new capacity control features
key_points: Athena Capacity Reservations get much smaller minimums: AWS reports 4 DPU (down from 24) for as little as 1 minute (down from 60), with up to 95% savings for workloads under an hour.
A one-click Step Functions autoscaler adjusts reserved DPU from CloudWatch utilisation, with an open-source template for custom rules such as business hours.
New per-workgroup and per-query minimum/maximum DPU limits, and each query now reports the DPU it used.
services: Amazon Athena, AWS Step Functions, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CloudFormation
decision: On-demand per-TB vs short, autoscaled capacity reservations (with DPU caps) for mixing interactive and scheduled Athena queries
authors: Manan Nayar, Mario Alkhoury, Pathik Shah, Saroj Yadav, Scott Rigney, Theo Tolv

title: How Zalando innovates their Fast-Serving layer by migrating to Amazon Redshift
key_points: Zalando replaced a legacy fast-serving warehouse with a producer/consumer Redshift setup: one producer loads data, consumer warehouses (provisioned for BI, Serverless for analysts) read it through data sharing; migrated in three stages: replicate, move workloads, decommission.

Lessons: automatic table optimisation only sees producer-side queries, so consumer workloads needed manual dist/sort keys and scheduled VACUUM; repeated CTEs were recomputed and became temp tables or MVs; oversized VARCHARs caused disk spill.
AWS reports Monday-morning report processing fell from 130 to 52 minutes and 75% of queries ran faster.
services: Amazon Redshift, Amazon Redshift Serverless, Redshift data sharing, Redshift Spectrum, Amazon MWAA, AWS Step Functions, AWS Lambda
decision: Single warehouse vs producer/consumer warehouses over data sharing, and who tunes tables for consumer-side workloads
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (measure VARCHAR sizing and CTE vs temp table/MV on Redshift Serverless); aws-bytes: data sharing (later)
authors: Zalando — Srinivasan Molkuva, Sabri Ömür Yıldırmaz, Prasanna Sudhindrakumar, Paritosh Kumar Pramanick, Saman Irfan, Werner Gunter

title: Using Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio Identity center (IDC) and IAM-based domains together
key_points: SageMaker Unified Studio has two domain types: Identity Center-based (per-user identity, governance, subscription workflows) and IAM-based (shared project role, newer developer tools).
Shows how a team keeps its governed Identity Center domain while also using an IAM-based domain, by reusing federated roles and attribute-based access control so subscriptions still apply.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS IAM Identity Center, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
authors: Praveen Kumar, Leonardo Gomez, Joel Farvault, Durga Mishra, Satish Sarapuri

title: Orchestrate end-to-end scalable ETL pipeline with Amazon SageMaker workflows
key_points: A daily Airflow DAG written inside SageMaker Unified Studio chains a Glue transform job, a Glue Data Quality job, an EMR Serverless notebook and a SQL notebook that loads Redshift Serverless.
The workflow environment is MWAA-backed but provisioned from the project, using the project role instead of separate per-service setup.
Long console-heavy setup; the takeaway is how a project-scoped orchestrator differs from a standalone MWAA or Step Functions setup.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon MWAA, Apache Airflow, AWS Glue, AWS Glue Data Quality, Amazon EMR Serverless, Amazon Redshift Serverless
decision: Standalone MWAA vs Step Functions vs SageMaker Unified Studio workflows for orchestrating Glue-to-Redshift batch pipelines
authors: Shubham Kumar, Nitin Kumar, Shubham Purwar

title: Reduce Mean Time to Resolution with an observability agent
key_points: An incident-investigation agent on Bedrock AgentCore queries logs and traces in OpenSearch and metrics in Managed Prometheus through MCP servers, correlating signals the way an SRE would.
Demo injects failures into a sample app and lets the agent find the root cause and estimate business impact; aimed at SRE teams, not data pipelines.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, OpenTelemetry
authors: Muthu Pitchaimani, Jon Handler

title: Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion 101: Set CloudWatch alarms for key metrics
key_points: Lists which CloudWatch metrics to alarm on for each part of an OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline: source, processors, buffer, sink and dead-letter queue.
Two worked scenarios: tracing where pipeline latency builds up, and fixing document rejections such as mapping errors and field-limit breaches.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon CloudWatch
authors: Utkarsh Agarwal, Ramesh Chirumamilla, Taylor Gray

title: Use Amazon MSK Connect and Iceberg Kafka Connect to build a real-time data lake
key_points: Debezium on MSK Connect reads the RDS for MySQL binlog into Kafka, and the open-source Iceberg Kafka sink (built from the Iceberg repo as a custom plugin) writes the changes into Iceberg tables on S3.
Runs in append mode, so the tables hold a change log rather than current state; shows single-table and multi-table routing and a column added at the source flowing through automatically.
Small-file compaction is left to Glue's table optimisation.
services: Amazon MSK, Amazon MSK Connect, Debezium, Apache Iceberg, Amazon RDS for MySQL, Amazon S3
decision: Debezium + Iceberg Kafka sink vs Firehose vs DMS for database CDC into Iceberg (change log vs current state)
attaches_to: aws-bytes: change data capture - DMS vs zero-ETL (later)
authors: Xiao Huang

title: Optimizing Flink’s join operations on Amazon EMR with Alluxio
key_points: Flink on EMR joins a Kafka order stream with Hive dimension tables; a plain lookup join keeps stale dimension data in state, needs full reloads and bloats checkpoints.
The fix caches the Hive dimension data in Alluxio and switches to a temporal table join so each event meets the dimension version valid at its time.
Hadoop/Hive-era stack; the managed-Flink enrichment patterns post covers the same problem more usefully.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache Flink, Alluxio, Apache Hive, Apache Kafka
authors: Qingyuan Tang

title: Federate access to Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio with AWS IAM Identity Center and Ping Identity
key_points: Console walkthrough for signing users into SageMaker Unified Studio with Ping Identity as the external identity provider, federated through IAM Identity Center over SAML.
Users and groups are provisioned automatically from Ping into Identity Center via SCIM; mostly identity-admin setup steps.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS IAM Identity Center, Ping Identity
authors: Raghavarao Sodabathina, Himanshu Sarda, Krupanidhi Jay, Nicholaus Lawson, Matt Nispel
